subject.title: macOS update can leave manual-update loop and stale node host causing Gateway restart storm

question: For macOS package updates already at the target version, should OpenClaw skip managed-service stop/restart by default while cleaning up duplicate submitted launchd updater jobs, or preserve same-version refresh semantics and solve only the stale-job supervisor loop?
rationale: Current tests intentionally refresh same-version package installs, but the live failure shows that behavior becomes destructive when launchd relaunches submitted updater jobs; automation should not choose that product policy silently.

options.title: Split and fix lifecycle policy
options.body: Default no-op package updates should avoid managed-service stop/restart, stale `manualupdate`/manual-update submitted jobs should be deduped and cleaned up, and a real macOS LaunchAgent smoke should prove recovery.

options.title: Preserve refresh semantics
options.body: Keep same-version package refresh as an explicit update behavior and narrowly repair submitted-job cleanup/dedupe so repeated launchd relaunches cannot keep killing the Gateway.

options.title: Defer to node-host fix only
options.body: Treat the node-host mismatch fix as sufficient and leave the manual updater-loop/no-op refresh behavior unchanged, accepting that the 2026.6.1 repro path remains possible.

recommendation.title: Split and fix lifecycle policy
recommendation.body: Default no-op package updates should avoid managed-service stop/restart, stale `manualupdate`/manual-update submitted jobs should be deduped and cleaned up, and a real macOS LaunchAgent smoke should prove recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice centers on package update service-state behavior, where this owner has adjacent merged history.
